summary: David Bradley is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a B.A. (Hons) from King's College London (1972-1975) and studied at the University of Cambridge (1975-1979).

David Brainerd Spooner (1879-1925) specialized in Indology and archaeology. Educated at Stanford, Tokyo, Sampurnanand Sanskrit, and Harvard (Ph.D.), he studied under Lanman, Pischel, and Marshall, and served in multiple director roles at the Archaeological Survey of India (1906, 1910, 1919).

David Brick is an Indologist who studied under Patrick Olivelle. He served on the editorial board of Anthem South Asian Normative Traditions Studies in 2012 and was a professor at Yale University (attested 2012-2018).

David Brown (1762-1812) worked in Indology and religious studies. Educated as a sizar at Magdalene College, Cambridge in 1782, he later served as Provost of Fort William College (~1800-1807) and founded the Calcutta Auxiliary Bible Society.

David Bubna-Litic earned his PhD from Western Sydney University. In 2000, he was a Lecturer in Strategic Management and Responsible Business at the University of Technology Sydney, with interests in Buddhist studies.

David Burton is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Bristol (1994-1997). He held posts at Keble College, Oxford (attested 2001) and Canterbury Christ Church University (attested 2010).

David Carpenter (born 1949) is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He served as Associate Professor of the History of Religions at Saint Joseph's University (~1987) and as Professor of Neurology at Washington University in St. Louis (2005).

David Dean Shulman (born 1949) is an Indologist who studied at Hebrew University of Jerusalem and under John Ralston Marr at SOAS, University of London. He spent his academic career at Hebrew University, becoming Professor of Indian Studies and Comparative Religion.

David Drewes is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Lawrence, Wisconsin-Madison, and Virginia (Ph.D. under Karen Christina Lang), he held teaching posts at Virginia, Indiana University Bloomington, and the University of Manitoba.

David E. Cooper (born 1942) is a philosopher educated at Oxford. He served as a Lecturer at the University of Oxford (1967), Professor of Philosophy at Durham University (1986-2008), and Distinguished International Visiting Professor at Peking University (2022).

David E. Riggs earned his Ph.D. from the University of California, Los Angeles, working in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He taught at UC Santa Barbara, UIUC, and UH Mānoa, and held research posts at Nichibunken and Oberlin College.

David Faure (born 1947) is a historian and sinologist. He studied at the University of Hong Kong and Princeton University (Ph.D.). He taught at Indiana University Bloomington, lectured at St Antony's College, and served as director at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

David Fiordalis is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. Educated at Carleton College, Chicago, and Michigan (Ph.D. under Luis Oscar Gómez), he served at Linfield University and as Research Editor for 84000: Translating the Words of the Buddha.

David Friedman (1903-1984) studied Indology and Buddhist studies at Utrecht, Leiden (Ph.D.), and Oxford. He taught at Leiden University, the University of Indonesia, SOAS University of London, and served as Professor at the University of London.

David Gellner (born 1957) is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held long-term posts at the University of Oxford, including All Souls College and Wolfson College, where he became Emeritus Professor of Social Anthropology.

David Germano is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1992 and was appointed Associate Professor of Tibetan and Buddhist Studies at the University of Virginia that same year.

David Gonsalez works in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He pursued his education under traditional teachers Lobsang Choephel, Lati Rinpoche, Kirti Tsenshab Rinpoche, and Denma Lochö Rinpoche.

David Goodman Mandelbaum (1911-1987) was an Indologist and anthropologist. He earned a B.A. from Northwestern and a Ph.D. from Yale under Edward Sapir, later serving at the University of Minnesota and the University of California, Berkeley.

David Gordon White (born 1953) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Wisconsin-Madison and Chicago (Ph.D.). He held academic appointments at the University of Virginia and the University of California, Santa Barbara.

David Higgins is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He worked as a researcher at the University of Vienna (attested 2015) and as a Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
